text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak says after a ministerial meeting: "Egypt wants to hold the economic conference on time and asks Israel and the United States to help make it a success... Turkey's Demirel denies having any troops in Iraq... We are continuing our contacts to support the Arab position."
- Mubarak and Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel Meguid discuss ways to implement the resolutions of the Cairo Summit.
- American warplanes in position to strike at military targets in Baghdad. C.N.N. says the strike will take place within 48 hours.

- Water level behind Aswan Dam has risen another 10 centimetres (four inches) to 176.56 metres. Minister of Culture says ancient stone temples on banks of Lake Nasser will not be affected by rising water.
- Mubarak says: "I told (Turkish President) Demirel that if he wanted a security zone (in Iraq) he should build it on his own territory."
- Police to use guard dogs to help secure the Egyptian Museum after a man tried to steal artefacts two days ago.
- Egypt objects to any interference in Iraq.
- Egypt and Kuwait to discuss setting up a free-trade zone.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to arrive in Cairo on Saturday for emergency Arab League meeting.
